articles.title: Football Daily - Carrick still in limbo & are Brighton title challengers? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Adam Crafton joins Rick and Lloyd to discuss Brighton, Man City and Man Utd.
articles.body:

Adam Crafton from The Athletic joins Rick Edwards and Lloyd Griffith after another Premier League weekend where Man Utd couldn’t keep themselves out of the headlines. Adam explains whether 4-4 is a good or bad result for Michael Carrick. Elsewhere, we discuss Man City’s downturn in form and whether this leaves Brighton as Arsenal’s closest title rivals. And Adam asks, if you were Fabian Hürzeler and Man Utd came knocking, would you leave Brighton? Get in touch with us via WhatsApp on 08000 289 369. articles.title: Barrenetxea no podrá ir con la Selección y le sustituye De Frutos
articles.standfirst: El 7 realista estará varias semanas K.O.
articles.summary: El 7 realista estará varias semanas K.O.
articles.body: Ander Barrenetxea no se incorporará hoy a la concentración de España para los partidos ante Chequia e Inglaterra, después de que el extremo de la Real Sociedad se tuviera que marchar lesionado del partido ante el Rayo Vallecano en el minuto 70, ayudado por dos médicos del equipo donostriarra y entre lágrimas, lo que hace pensar que sufre un problema muscular lo suficientemente grave como para impedirle unirse al equipo de Luis de la Fuente. Su puesto en la convocatoria lo asume Jorge de Frutos, extremo del Rayo Vallecano, que se incorporará a la concentración de la Selección este lunes 9 de noviembre a partir de las 13 horas en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas. “Tenemos que esperar a las pruebas médicas, pero parece de los isquios”, decía Matarazzo al acabar el partido. “Ojalá que sea poco porque le necesitamos pronto”, añadió Remiro. ‘Barrene’, que estaba siendo uno de los mejores del partido y se encontraba en buena forma, notó el tirón después de ser clave en el primer gol del partido, asistiendo con un gran pase a Óskarsson para que se quedara solito ante Audero, al que batió. Pero le duró poco la alegría a la Real, porque acto seguido el extremo se tuvo que marchar lesionado, dejando su sitio a Ochieng. El 7 realista no fue el único que sufrió un problema así, porque en la parte final del partido el rayista Vertrouwd tuvo que ser reemplazado al poco de salir al césped de Anoeta. Luis de la Fuente ha premiado el gran momento de Jorge De Frutos con su convocatoria para el próximo parón de selecciones. Esta será la tercera convocatoria del de Navares de Enmedio con la Selección Española. Ya hizo su debut el 7 de septiembre de 2025 en la goleada por 0-6 ante Turquía en la que jugó algo más de 22 minutos. Beñat ya lo adelantó en la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro ante la Real. “Si el seleccionador no lo ha llevado, seguro que lo tendrá en su lista”. Efectivamente. De Frutos tendrá que luchar ahora por un puesto de cara a los encuentros ante República Checa (12 de noviembre) e Inglaterra (15 de noviembre).

articles.title: AP Top 25: Georgia moves to No. 1 after Notre Dame's win over Miami, Ohio State drops out of top 20
articles.summary: The Bulldogs demolished Ole Miss on Saturday.
articles.body:
Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the AP Top 25.

The Bulldogs took over the top spot after No. 1 Miami lost at Notre Dame on Saturday night. The Hurricanes fell to No. 5, behind Georgia, Utah, Notre Dame and UCLA.

Georgia blew out Ole Miss on Saturday and were the obvious choice to move up a spot. Utah beat BYU to move up to No. 2 , while UCLA won on the road at Minnesota.

Utah and UCLA are the only two remaining undefeated teams at the top level of college football.

The rest of the top 10 is filled out by Indiana, Alabama, Texas, Tennessee and Texas Tech. The Crimson Tide won at LSU on Saturday, while Tennessee had a dominant win over a Kentucky team that hadn't lost since Week 2 against Alabama.

Ohio State dropped all the way to No. 21 after losing at home to Oregon. The Buckeyes gave up 41 points in the loss and may be without a playoff path now that they have three losses.

Wake Forest is up to No. 11 as the second ACC team in the rankings. The Demon Deacons played FCS-level Merrimack on Saturday.

In Week 11, No. 2 Utah goes to No. 22 Arizona, No. 15 USC visits No. 6 Indiana and No. 8 Texas heads to No. 24 LSU. And we'll see on Tuesday night how much difference there is between the AP poll and the second set of College Football Playoff rankings. A week ago, Notre Dame was seven spots lower in the CFP rankings than it was in the AP Top 25.

articles.title: Julián falló el 1-0 en un claro mano a mano... pero lo arregló regalando a Giuliano el primer gol del partido
articles.standfirst: El argentino, protagonista en el Metropolitano
articles.summary: El argentino, protagonista en el Metropolitano
articles.body: Julián tuvo un inicio de partido ajetreado. En un duelo en el que todos los focos iban a estar sobre él por el contencioso que tuvieron Atlético y Barcelona por él en verano, el argentino salió con las pilas puestas. El 19 del Atleti tuvo la primera ocasión del partido, clarísima, en un mano a mano en el minuto 6 en el que corrió muchos metros libre antes de encarar a un Joan García al que intentó regatear pero al que no pudo desbordar. Julián falló un gol clarísimo para desesperación de la parroquia del Metropolitano, aunque lo arregló pronto. Un par de minutos después, volvió a tener protagonismo en el área. Kang-in hizo un cambio de juego con el exterior para Julián, de banda a banda, y el argentino vio la llegada de Giuliano, que remató de primeras en el área para batir a Joan García y poner el 1-0 en el marcador. Julián tuvo otra ocasión en el segundo tiempo, con un intento de vaselina lejana en otra acción en la que un pase al espacio le dejó solito ante Joan García, pero el argentino no quiso correr al área y buscó definir de lejos por arriba... sin puntería. Tras la derrota, Julián Alvarez estuvo junto al resto del equipo en el agradecimiento a la afición, aplaudiendo a la grada.

articles.title: Bizarre & thrilling theatre as Carrick's Man Utd future still in limbo
articles.summary: It was a Premier League classic at Old Trafford but what as Man Utd's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa done to Michael Carrick's future?
articles.body:
After yet another breathless, chaotic, shambolic Old Trafford classic, Manchester United do not know whether to laugh or cry.

Their fans didn't, booing at some points, cheering at others.

Defender Diogo Dalot was singled out for gruesome treatment amid the second-half protests and songs of defiance as he was replaced by Patrick Dorgu in the 66th minute.

The players didn't, running away joyously to celebrate Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser that made it 4-4 against Aston Villa. They then applauded the supporters who stayed on despite the apparent hopelessness of the situation as the game entered injury-time with United trailing 4-2, presumably to vent their anger on a day when defeat seemed certain.

Manager Michael Carrick was in spiky mood when he was quizzed about his future by Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison.

"That's not going to happen," he said, when asked if he was going to walk away.

"Will there?" Carrick then added, when it was suggested there would 'clearly be conversations' with United's hierarchy.

"You're telling me what you think," he responded.

"I'm quite clear what direction the club needs to go in. It's got to win games."

Sunday's ridiculous eight-goal thriller with Villa - a game in which the hosts fought back twice from two goals down - left United 18th in the table and in the Premier League drop zone.

As they enter the international break, they will spend more time in the relegation zone than they have done since 1986.

United have not won a league game since they beat Ipswich on August 30, have conceded 15 goals in their last five games and conceded inside two minutes in three of their last seven matches.

Three minutes and 40 seconds was the earliest they have ever trailed 2-0 in a Premier League game.

Up next is a trip to Anfield to play rivals Liverpool on 22 November.

On the positive side, United's players have not downed tools for their manager.

Somehow, despite being two goals down on three occasions in the last two games, they have emerged with a win and a draw.

Added to a creditable first-half display in a 2-0 loss at Chelsea on 31 October where they had Lisandro Martinez sent off, before which Carrick was backed to turn the current situation round, was that enough for Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family - and detached from this latest crazy day?

Was it enough for chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox who were at Old Trafford?

"On the one hand it's dreadful to give up four goals at home," former United skipper Roy Keane told Sky Sports. "But they kept going, so you have to give them a little bit of praise.

"In terms of the bigger picture it's that rollercoaster of watching Manchester United. When you turn up most weeks there really is the feeling of not knowing what you're going to get."

Former United striker Dion Dublin offered his own take on BBC Sport as he added: "There's only so many times you can do that because it's quite tiring, physically and mentally. The players today were walking around after the game like they had lost, even though they got a point."

Some of the post-match interviews by United players backed up that observation.

"I don't feel happy - we are in a bad situation," admitted Dorgu. "We need to fight together to get out of it.

"Everyone needs to look at themselves and ask if they are doing enough. We need to fight for the manager, for the club and get out of this together."

The situation has not been made easier by fan sentiment.

Lack of form on the pitch, combined with rising cost of ticket prices and a negative perception of how fans are being treated, has led to a negative reaction that is unprecedented in its ferocity since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

A banner was hung from the second tier of the Stretford End shortly before the teams came out to start the game. It read 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners'.

Full-back Dalot was jeered off the pitch when he was replaced by Dorgu, the catcalls replacing the cheers that greeted his number being shown.

Joshua Zirkzee, who scored United's third in the second minute of injury time, suffered similar treatment during a game against Newcastle almost two years ago. The Netherlands forward was still on the bench when Dalot arrived and offered his team-mate a consoling hug.

'We're just making it too difficult for ourselves'

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was livid by his side's late capitulation, which cost him a first victory at Old Trafford.

Touted as a potential successor to Carrick, he regathered his composure after storming down the tunnel before the final whistle to assure United fans the club's results will improve.

"They have the capacity, power, players and everything to overcome this situation," said the Spaniard.

That is probably true. But from so many angles, the current position remained grim.

The Villa game was like a number so far this season - Everton away, Atletico Madrid away, Tottenham at home, Leeds away, Chelsea away - where either United have played well, or got themselves into winning positions in stoppage time and failed to secure victory.

Although the present situation can still be rectified, it now needs two lots of results to go Carrick's way for the table to look more positive. Yet how long will it be before it is accepted that such anticipated improvement is not going to materialise?

Can United afford to wait until the January window opens? Have they got the resources to spend in it when it does?

These are bound to feed into the thinking of Ratcliffe, the Glazers, Berrada and Wilcox as they consider the future; plus the attractiveness of potential replacements.

For now, Carrick is still looking to a future he is certain will be brighter than what he has just endured.

"There's more than enough," he said, when asked if he had seen enough to believe the current situation can be improved.

"Goals change games and you've got to deal with it. It's something we have to improve on drastically. We're just making it too difficult for ourselves at certain times.

"They (players) are switched on and concentrated, it's a variety of things. There's not a theme to it, apart from these one-off moments are catching us out at the moment."
authors: Simon Stone - Manchester United reporter at Old Trafford

articles.title: Joe Burrow overpowers Falcons as Bengals win in Madrid
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals got an outstanding performance from their star quarterback on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals got an outstanding performance from their star quarterback on Sunday.

Joe Burrow threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns as the Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons, 34-17, at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain.

Ja'Marr Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown. Tee Higgins had five catches, including two scores.

The Falcons took a 7-0 lead as Michael Penix Jr. found Charlie Woerner for a 1-yard touchdown. The Bengals responded as Burrow threw a 47-yard touchdown pass to Chase to even the score at 7-7.

Nick Folk made a 31-yard field goal to give Atlanta a 10-7 advantage after one quarter.

Burrow's 1-yard touchdown run put Cincinnati ahead, 14-10. Higgins' 4-yard touchdown catch and Evan McPherson's 57-yard field goal extended it to 24-10 at halftime.

Bijan Robinson's 1-yard touchdown run cut the deficit to 24-17. But the Bengals answered as the Burrow found Higgins for an 8-yard touchdown to extend it to 31-17.

McPherson capped the scoring with a 43-yard field goal.

Burrow went 24-of-29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns. The Bengals also ran for 123 yards.

Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh on Nov. 15 at Paycor Stadium for Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: El Colo Colo de Vozinha y Vidal, campeón de Chile: "Esto culmina todo lo que he hecho durante toda mi vida"
articles.standfirst: Bolados dio este domingo el título a los suyos con un gol agónico en el 93'
articles.summary: Bolados dio este domingo el título a los suyos con un gol agónico en el 93'
articles.body: Con un gol agónico en el minuto 93. Marcos Bolados dio este domingo al Colo Colo, en el que juega el portero 'Vozinha', su título 35 de la liga chilena, tras vencer por 1-2 en su visita al Ñublense y consagrarse campeón con tres fechas de anticipación al cierre del campeonato. Cuando el partido se extinguía, una pelota centrada al área que alcanzó a tocar el delantero argentino Javier Correa quedó flotando para que Bolados, deslizándose, la mandara dentro del arco perseguido por dos defensores. Bolados dio el trofeo a los albos, pero también al técnico argentino Fernando Ortiz, para quien es la primera corona de su carrera como entrenador, y al portero de Cabo Verde 'Vozinha', que alcanzó su primer campeonato jugando en el extranjero. La suerte del Cacique cambió en un giro inesperado, luego de que todo apuntaba a que la definición se extendería una jornada porque el Ñublense, que peleaba por meterse en la zona de clasificación a la Copa Sudamericana, formó una muralla atrás para evitar que el dominio albo terminara en gol. El partido había comenzado con el ídolo del club Arturo Vidal tomando el protagonismo para abrir el marcador, en el minuto 14, con una volea que reventó el arco del portero uruguayo Nicola Pérez. La ventaja, no obstante, duró poco porque casi sobre la media hora la zaga de los albos dejó solo a Lucas Molina en el punto de penalti para patear una pelota que vino desde un saque lateral, y así fusilar a 'Vozinha'. A partir de ahí, el Colo Colo dominó el juego, pero no lograba convertir, mientras que su escolta Universidad de Chile ganaba ante el Cobresal por 2-1 y achicaba la diferencia a ocho puntos en la tabla. Así apareció Bolados, para concretar los tres puntos que dejan a los albos con 61 unidades en la cima, con 10 de ventaja sobre la U, que ya no puede alcanzarle, pero que se afirma en la segunda plaza que le da un puesto directo a la próxima Copa Libertadores, en la que el Colo Colo ya anotó su nombre. El cuadro de Ortiz logró el objetivo a falta de tres fechas para el final del campeonato, tras haber visto extinguirse una parte de su ventaja en el liderato, con cuatro fechas sin ganar hasta que en la pasada jornada volvió al triunfo con una goleada. Con el título definido, la liga tendrá ahora una lucha final entre la U de Chile -con 51 enteros- y Universidad Católica por la plaza directa a la Libertadores, con apenas dos puntos de diferencia entre ambos y nueve por disputar. El Colo Colo, por su parte, ahora encara la Copa Chile en la que está clasificado a semifinales. "Vine aquí para eso, para ganar el título y gracias a Dios conseguimos lograr este gran título. Estoy muy feliz y muy contento", dijo el portero al terminar el encuentro contra el Ñublense. El guardameta, de 40 años, fue titular en la victoria como visitantes de los albos por 1-2 que significó el trofeo 35 en la historia del Colo Colo. 'Vozinha' le dedicó el título a su familia. "(Esto es para) toda mi familia, para todo Cabo Verde, mis compañeros y para todos los hinchas de Colo Colo", afirmó. Para 'Vozinha' es el título más importante de su carrera, en la que solo había conseguido un campeonato con el Mindelense de su país y una Copa Chipre con el AEL Limassol. "Pienso que culmina todo lo que he hecho durante toda mi vida, toda mi carrera y estoy muy feliz por eso", destacó en una entrevista a TNT Sports. Tras emerger en el Mundial 2026, en el que firmó grandes actuaciones contra España y Argentina, Vozinha corona un semestre en el que también estuvo nominado al premio al mejor portero en la gala del Balón de Oro. El arquero caboverdiano fue protagonista en la última jugada del duelo de este domingo, al detener un remate esquinado que habría sido el empate del equipo de Chillán. "Es el trabajo de todo el equipo durante todo el campeonato, llegué aquí cuando faltaban muy pocos juegos, pero estoy siempre para ayudar. También fallé en algunos momentos, erré, pero eso es parte de fútbol y ahora pienso celebrar", comentó. El caboverdiano llegó al Colo Colo a inicios de agosto recién iniciada la segunda vuelta del campeonato y su adaptación fue lenta, pues tras su arribo el técnico de los albos, el argentino Fernando Ortiz, no le ofreció una continuidad bajo el arco. El portero, sin embargo, retribuyó a todo el equipo luego de alcanzar el objetivo. "Antes de más quiero agradecer a todos mis compañeros, la dirigencia, staff técnico y a todos los trabajadores de Colo Colo, que me han recibido muy bien desde el primer día", afirmó. El título le aseguró al Colo Colo un lugar en la próxima Copa Libertadores. Vozinha firmó un contrato solo por seis meses, que vencerá en diciembre próximo, pero contempla una cláusula de extensión automática si disputa al menos el 50 % de los minutos que juegue el equipo en el período establecido en el acuerdo. Tras este partido, registra 540 minutos en cancha y el cálculo contempla que al Colo Colo le restan 450 de juego considerando los tres partidos de liga más los dos de la semifinal de la Copa Chile, de los cuales tendría que ser titular en dos y jugar al menos 45 minutos más. Ante este panorama, Vozinha solo dijo: "Hoy es día de celebrar, después hablamos del futuro".

articles.title: Oregon Ducks' chances to make CFP skyrocket after win, per ESPN FPI
articles.summary: With the Oregon Ducks' win over the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday, their chances at making the College Football Playoff have skyrocketed.
articles.body:
Don't look now, but the Oregon Ducks season might be back on track, with expectations returning.

After a huge blowout win over the Ohio State Buckeyes in Columbus over the weekend, Dan Lanning's team kept its season alive, with real hopes of making the Big Ten Championship and potentially the College Football Playoff.

With three games left, Oregon has a decent chance to reach the Big Ten title game if it wins out, and even a chance to earn an at-large CFP bid when all is said and done. That much is reflected in the latest look at ESPN's Football Power Index.

Going into the weekend, Oregon had just a 4.2% chance to make the playoff, but that number skyrocketed to 24.9% after the win in Columbus. Nothing is possible unless the Ducks win their final three games, but at this point, it's reasonable to say there is a chance.

Here's a look at the new ESPN FPI numbers and what they mean for the Ducks.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 85.9%

Analysis: What looked like a very tough game at the start of the year has really lost some of its luster. Oregon is starting to click at the right time, while Michigan is watching the wheels fall off. After a loss to the Michigan State Spartans over the weekend, the Kyle Whittingham era may be headed for a quick end, as the Ducks are now double-digit favorites in this game at home.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 84.4%

Analysis: Despite the Spartans' big win over Michigan over the weekend, it doesn't all of a sudden make them a major threat in this game. While it is a road game on a short week for Oregon, I still think they will be favored by double digits and should be able to come out on top should they play with the level of success that we've seen over the past couple of weeks.

Oregon Percent Chance to Win, Per ESPN FPI: 86.7%

Analysis: Washington may not be playing for much in this game, but Oregon could potentially be trying to keep its season alive, whether that be in the race for a spot in the Big Ten Championship game or an at-large bid into the College Football Playoff. The Huskies have been struggling mightily this season, so the Ducks should be favored by quite a bit going into this game.

Percent Chance to Make College Football Playoff: 24.9%

Percent Chance to Make National Championship: 2.0%

Percent Chance to Win National Championship: 0.8%

articles.title: 'Campeonissimos': España gana la 'Finalissima' en y ante Brasil (0-3)
articles.standfirst: En un gran segundo tiempo, Gon Castejón, Cecilio y Antonio Pérez sellan el triunfo
articles.summary: En un gran segundo tiempo, Gon Castejón, Cecilio y Antonio Pérez sellan el triunfo
articles.body: La Selección española sigue su paso firme, con Jesús Velasco, y a la Supercopa conquistada en febrero en Liubliana suma desde hoy la 'Finalissima' tras imponerse a la gran final a Brasil (0-3) en Niterói. Brasil y España vivieron una auténtica batalla de desgaste desde que los colegiados uruguayos Daniel Rodríguez y Andrés Martínez pitaron el inicio del partido. Ambos combinados nacionales eran conscientes de la transcendencia del encuentro era incluso mayor que el trofeo de la 'Finalissima' que estaba en juego. Salieron mucho mejor los de Marquinhos Xavier con una presión alta y tratando de finalizar todas las acciones contra la portería, que empezó defendiendo Dídac Plana. El portero del Barça tuvo que estar muy fino en tres acciones, ante Arthur, Pito y Lucas Gómez. España tuvo la más clara en las zapatillas de Antonio Pérez, pero apareció Willian, confirmando que Brasil también tiene un superportero. El nivel arbitral fue mucho menos permisivo que en las semifinales, lo que posibilitó que ambos equipos se vieran pronto amenazados por las cinco faltas, pero en los 20 primeros minutos, ninguna las incurrió, lo que no impidió que España y Brasil jugaran un partido al máximo nivel sin que, eso sí, el marcador se moviera en los primeros 20 minutos. Tras el descanso, España comenzó mejor, lo que llevó, cuando apenas se habían jugado siete minutos a Marquinhos Xavier a pedir tiempo muerto. Fue psicológico, porque los suyos empezaron a llegar con más claridad de lo que lo habían hecho hasta ese momento. Sin embargo, la Selección tuvo capacidad de reacción y una recuperación de Gon Castejón, propició que condujera Antonio Pérez y el propio Gon Castejón llegara para finalizar. La presión final de Brasil fue asfixiante, no obstante el 3-2 con Marcel como portero jugador propiciaba que España tuviera opciones de salir al contraataque y, en una de ellas, Cecilio encontró la puerta vacía brasileña para hacer el segundo. A falta de 33.7 segundos los colegiados pitaron penalti de Adolfo sobre Pito. No hubo expulsión, pero el FICHA TÉCNICA Niterói Arena, 2.600 espectadores. articles.title: Koke: "Tuvimos ocasiones para matar el partido y no lo hicimos..."
articles.standfirst: El capitán rojiblanco analizó la derrota de los suyos ante el Barcelona
articles.summary: El capitán rojiblanco analizó la derrota de los suyos ante el Barcelona
articles.body: El capitán del Atlético fue uno de los futbolistas más destacados de los de Simeone en el duelo ante el Barcelona. Koke, que regresó a la titularidad, analizó el partido en los micrófonos de Movistar al acabar el duelo. Qué ha decidido el partido: "La efectividad. El equipo ha hecho un gran primer tiempo, tuvimos ocasiones para matar el partido y no lo hicimos. Con un disparo y un rebote al final del primer tiempo nos hicieron el gol. El fútbol es así, es contundencia y ellos han sido más contundentes que nosotros. Nada que reprochar al equipo. Hay que seguir así, que queda mucha Liga. Hay que seguir y no quedarse con la derrota". No pasaba nada en el partido y ha llegado el segundo gol, que nos ha hecho daño". Dos derrotas seguidas: "Con ganas de jugar el siguiente partido y ganarlo". Barrios: "Pablo es un grandísimo jugador. articles.title: Falkirk add goals and grit to John McGlynn's guile on rapid rise
articles.summary: Falkirk continue to excel under the canny guidance of John McGlynn as a run of five successive victories takes them up to third in the Scottish Premiership.
articles.body:
In the space of a week Falkirk have beaten defending champions Celtic and become the first team to get the better of Hearts in a Scottish Premiership match at Tynecastle in 19 months, scoring a combined seven goals in the process.

The 5-2 success in Edinburgh was their fifth successive victory and takes John McGlynn's side up to third place.

A month ago, the concession of an added time goal to Dundee left them 11th, only a point off the bottom of the table.

"It's striking a balance without getting carried away and not playing it down too much," McGlynn told BBC Scotland.

"Winning five games in a row, you've obviously got something about you. We want it to continue because we're enjoying this.

"But we're only 13 games in. There's a long way to go, so we've got to keep our feet on the ground and enjoy seeing our team third in the league."

The 64-year-old earned plaudits aplenty last season for guiding Falkirk to sixth on their return to the top flight after overseeing consecutive promotions.

Liam Henderson, who scored the sublime fourth goal against Hearts, was with the Bairns in those League One days, as were Brad Spencer and Ethan Ross.

Unused substitutes Finn Yeats and Ross MacIver have been on the journey with McGlynn too, as has Leon McCann, who missed out through injury.

"We've got a good team spirit, a togetherness, and a will to work hard for your team-mates," said centre-half Henderson. "We now have a ruthlessness up front as well.

"The manager is massive to us. His knowledge, his detail. He is so detailed in everything he does.

"We're breaking records this season and creating some history. A lot of pundits and fans were saying that we weren't the team we were last year."

There is truth to that. While some of the old guard remain, there was a huge squad turnover in the summer.

Calvin Miller went to Hearts, Dylan Tait is now the skipper at Dundee United and Barney Stewart, who scored 10 goals between January and May, was sold to West Bromwich Albion for a club record fee.

Loan players Filip Lissah, Ben Broggio, Henry Cartwright, Kyrell Wilson, Ethan Williams and Louie Marsh said their goodbyes.

McGlynn brought in a whopping 17 new faces, with Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames and Jacob Murrell, who all scored against Hearts, arriving weeks after the campaign had kicked off.

Murrell, 22, picked up the SPFL player of the month award for October and his Tynecastle double takes his tally to seven, making him joint-top scorer in the division.

"They look at what kind of player fits into the team and when the player arrives, they know what they're getting," said former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart in praise of Falkirk's scouting.

Meanwhile, former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan highlighted captain Spencer as the "heartbeat" of the team.

"You need a guy like him in there to really set the standards," Allan said of the 30-year-old midfielder, who followed McGlynn from Raith Rovers.

"When he is in the team, there is a real control from Falkirk, especially in the middle.

"They've added a steeliness to the team too, it's not always total football this year. They are able to do the dirty side of the game now and roll up the sleeves when they have to."

McGlynn is very much the unassuming star of the show though.

"He is a manager who is totally comfortable in his own skin now," said Stewart.

"He exudes confidence. Perhaps before he was considered a bit of an unfashionable manager. I mean in terms of stature, and not in what he's doing on the park.

"The perception of him continues to get better and better.

"I don't want to be disrespectful to Falkirk, but I would not be surprised, if, when one or two of the bigger jobs start coming up, rather than being an outsider, I think he will be right in the hunt for some of those."

As things stand, almost any move away from Falkirk would be a step down the league.

articles.title: Las verdades de Frenkie de Jong
articles.standfirst: La opinión de Jaime Rincón
articles.summary: La opinión de Jaime Rincón
articles.body: Pocos jugadores han generado tanto debate en la época reciente en Can Barça como Frenkie de Jong. El neerlandés suele ser blanco habitual de las críticas en el entorno culé. En las últimas temporadas, por sus recurrentes lesiones, especialmente cuando el origen acontece durante las ventanas de selección. Sin embargo, no creo que sea un futbolista del que se pueda poner en duda su compromiso. Siempre ha dado la cara. Siempre. Pero la sensación con Frenkie, al menos la de sus detractores, es que puede parecer un centrocampista intrascendente. Los números avalan esa teoría. No tiene llegada, no tiene gol y pese a ser un mediocentro creativo, tampoco lidera la clasificación de máximos asistentes. Ningún año lo ha hecho. Pero, por fortuna, el fútbol no siempre se explica desde los números. A todos ellos, entre los que me puedo incluir durante algunas fases de su estancia en Barcelona, les pondría el partido del Metropolitano para entender qué le da Frenkie a un equipo como el Barça. Antes de desentrañar los intangibles del neerlandés en una época donde el Big Data está de moda, adelanto la conclusión: el Barcelona es mejor equipo con Frenkie que sin él. Así de simple. Flick recurrió a él como lateral. Hubo quien se frotó los ojos tras el descanso. Frenkie de lateral derecho. Inaudito. Y cortó la hemorragia en esa banda por donde se desangró el Barça en el primer tiempo. Y después pasó al mediocampo. Porque Frenkie te vale para un roto y para un descosido. Tiene despliegue físico, es habitual ganador de duelos y no pierde un balón ni a tiros. Y por ahí empezó a ganar el partido del Metropolitano el Barça. El equipo de Flick se quedó el balón, lo monopolizó hasta el punto que el Atlético se quedó sin opciones de transición. La única vez que desnudó al Barça en el segundo tiempo -en el primero se hartó de hacerlo- fue por una pérdida de Fermín con el equipo iniciando jugada en el mediocampo. La de la vaselina de Julián. Y todo vino por el pase de seguridad que garantizó Frenkie. La superioridad que provocó en el mediocampo. Siempre encuentra el espacio para conducir, la pausa para frenar la jugada. Le sobra experiencia. Le sobra calidad. Ni un mal control, ni una mala decisión que generase un potencial peligro. Tranquilizó al Barça con balón. De una manera exagerada. Y mientras se nos llena la boca a todos los españoles con Rodri, con todos los motivos para hacerlo, Frenkie es un sospechoso habitual. Y el español tampoco asiste ni marca. Casi nunca. Quizá el problema, o uno de ellos, radica en pensar que Frenkie no es un 5 y sí un falso interior. Es comprensible porque su potencia en la conducción, la que le permite superar líneas de presión con abrumadora facilidad, puede inducir a error. Es así de bueno. Y lo ha sido siempre. Por eso lo fichó el Barça y por eso todos los entrenadores lo ponen. Todos.

articles.summary: La hija de Pepe Mel
articles.body: La familia Mel está viviendo días complicados después de que el pasado día 1 de noviembre Pepe Mel sufriera una accidente cerebrovascular, por le que tuvo que ser intervenido quirúrgicamente en un hospital de Sevilla. El que fuera entrenador de equipos como el Betis, Deportivo de La Coruña, Las Palmas y Tenerife (entre otro equipos) continúa ingresado en el hospital Virgen del Rocío de la capital hispalense donde está siendo tratado, mientras que su mujer y su hija Iris Mel siguen al minuto al evolución de Pepe Mel, confiando en que los tratamientos que le están suministrando produzcan una evolución positiva. Precisamente, Iris Mel ha publicado en su cuenta de Instagram un emotivo mensaje dirigido a su padre, con el que demuestra la unión tan especial que tienen entre ambos. La publicación va acompañada de una fotografía de padre e hija en la que ambos sonríen durante una reunión familiar. "Sé que vas a volver conmigo, lo sé porque me prometiste que íbamos hacer más cosas juntos, y tú me enseñaste que las promesas se tienen que cumplir. Nos quedan muchas ciudades que conocer, muchos países que visitar y mucha historia que aprender. Necesito que sigas recomendándome libros para leer por las noches, que discutamos por cómo está la sociedad a día de hoy y de donde deberíamos comer". "No puede ser que nuestra última visita sea sin darnos un beso porque te podía pegar algo. No sé qué puede ser de nosotras dos sin ti, no sé ni quiero. No me dejes aquí sola porque me prometiste que siempre estarías para mí, lucha por nosotras".

articles.title: Michigan's Jason Beck Fired Amid Kyle Whittingham Hot-Seat Buzz, Was CFB's Highest-Paid OC
articles.summary: Michigan is making changes.
articles.body:
The Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck following Saturday's 15-6 loss to Michigan State.

ESPN's Pete Thamel and The Athletic's Bruce Feldman and Austin Meek first reported the news

Per The Athletic's report, head coach Kyle Whittingham "brought Beck from Utah and made him the highest-paid OC in the country at $3 million per season. Beck's offense was supposed to bring out the best in five-star quarterback Bryce Underwood, who is also earning roughly $3 million per year, but the pairing never clicked."

Michigan's offense has been absolutely brutal this season. The team ranks tied for 226th in passing offense (173.9 YPG), 109th in rushing offense (128.7 YPG) and 126th in scoring (19.6 PPG).

If it wasn't for a stout defense—and an extremely controversial Hail Mary against Western Michigan—the Wolverines might be far worse than an already-disappointing 5-4 record.

Even more troubling is that Underwood, the top overall recruit in the Class of 2025, has been so poor under Beck that he was bench midseason and replaced by Tommy Carr.

Even with the Wolverines struggling against Michigan State, Underwood remained on the sidelines.

"That was a conversation. Whether or not Bryce should go in late in the third quarter. Should that switch be made? Just felt like it wasn't going to be the answer if we would have done that. In hindsight, maybe we should have done that," Whittingham told reporters following Saturday's loss. "But we've got some serious issues. I don't know what else to say other than we're not going to just give up on the season. We've got three games left. We've got some kids in that locker room who have a lot of pride and a lot of want-to. We just got to find a way to get back on track."

The hope will be that offensive line coach Jim Harding can provide some answers in that regard as he takes over as interim offensive coordinator.

articles.body: Fermín López está en un excelente momento. Es un jugador decisivo y desequilibrante. Rompedor. El internacional andaluz festejó en el Metropolitano su partido 100 en LaLiga confirmando su extraordinario rendimiento: volvió a ser determinante en ataque. Un partido más. Fermín López fue uno de los realizadores y protagonistas de la jornada. El profesional de El Campillo marcó dos goles. Con el primero ponía el empate a uno en el cruce contra el Atlético de Madrid. El segundo tanto, tras asistencia de Lamine Yamal, implicó que el Barcelona se adelantara en el marcador y lograra finalmente un éxito que le mantiene como líder de Primera. El medio sólo se quedó sin ser decisivo en el Clásico del Spotify Camp Nou. Pero asistió contra el PSG; dio dos pases finales y vio puerta frente al Alavés; habilitó a Raphinha en uno de sus tantos contra el Aston Villa; y en el Metropolitano superó a Oblak y a la férrea zaga rojiblanca en dos ocasiones. El centrocampista andaluz, de 23 años, ya suma siete tantos en LaLiga, uno más que los que rubricó en todo el torneo doméstico en las dos últimas campañas. En la 23-24, logró ocho. Además, ha dado cinco asistencias. En total, contando también la Champions League, su balance hasta la fecha es de 9 dianas y siete pases finales. El canterano azulgrana, que ya ha defendido la camiseta culé en 151 encuentros, se ha convertido en un hombre fundamental en el esquema de Hansi Flick. En los primeros cruces, el técnico alemán iba alternando a Fermín y a Olmo en la mediapunta, pero la lesión del de Terrassa le ha dado aún más protagonismo. Su campaña está siendo sobresaliente.

articles.title: Lopez double fires Barcelona to win at Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Fermin Lopez brace has Barcelona come from behind to win 2-1 at Atletico Madrid to go three points clear in La Liga.
articles.body:
Fermin Lopez scored twice as Barcelona overcame an early deficit at Atletico Madrid to win 2-1 and go three points clear at the top of La Liga.

Barca’s win takes them three points clear of second-placed Real Madrid and five ahead of Atletico, in third, after 12 games.

Giuliano Simeone opened the scoring in the 10th minute for the home side, turning home a close range volley from Julian Alvarez’s cross from the left.

The home side had a series of early chances as they sought to register an eighth straight win, but Fermin swept in an equaliser on the cusp of halftime after a ball broke to him in the box.

Lamine Yamal set up Fermin’s second goal in the 66th minute with an incisive pass, and Lopez fired past Jan Oblak with a first-time finish to silence the Metropolitano and secure a fifth straight away league win over Atleti for the first time.

“It was a very difficult match. The first half was tough, but we managed to come from behind and secure the win,” Barcelona midfielder Lopez told La Liga TV after the match.

“I think we were not being clinical enough. After the goal, we gained more confidence.

“Lamine [Yamal] has been very good. His pass for the second goal was half the goal itself. I’m very happy,” Lopez said.

“We wanted to go into the break as league leaders and get three points. The equaliser lifted a weight off our shoulders, and we had more control.

“We knew at halftime that we had to continue playing the way we finished the first half. I think the team produced an incredible second half, both defensively and offensively. We’re very happy.”

articles.title: Michigan fires offensive coordinator Jason Beck after 15-6 loss to Michigan State
articles.summary: Beck was the highest-paid offensive coordinator in the nation, yet Michigan ranked second-to-last in the Big Ten in scoring offense.
articles.body:
Michigan has fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, the football program announced on Sunday .

The dismissal comes after the Wolverines' 15-6 loss to Michigan State on Saturday night, during which Michigan only generated 192 yards of offense and didn't score until getting a touchdown with 1:55 remaining in the game.

Offensive line coach Jim Harding is expected to take over the OC role in the interim, according to On3's Pete Nakos .

During Beck's nine games as OC, Michigan ranked No. 132 out of 138 FBS teams in total offense with 2,723 yards. Scoring an average of 19.6 points per game, the Wolverines were the 13th-worst team in the nation .

"The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense," Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said in a statement . "We need to put our offensive players and the entire team in the best possible position to be successful."

A national search for a new offensive coordinator will be conducted, according to Michigan.

Beck was the highest-paid offensive coordinator in the nation, earning a reported $3 million annual salary on his three-year contract. Michigan owes him $10.1 million for the remainder of his deal, pending him getting another coaching job elsewhere, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.

'At some point, you've got to have results'

Following the loss to Michigan State, Whittingham was asked if he would consider replacing Beck after the offense's poor production throughout the season.

"Not right now. Not as I'm sitting here at this podium, no," Whittingham said. "But at some point, you've got to have results. It's a result-driven business, and it's a bottom line business." "I'll evaluate everything after the season and determine what the best course of action is," he added. "But not right here, right now."

After one season as OC with Utah, Beck followed Whittingham to Michigan. During the 2025 season, the Utes ranked fourth in the nation in total offense and points per game (41.1). Prior to joining Whittingham's staff, Beck had offensive coordinator stints at Syracuse and New Mexico.

With 16 years of coaching quarterbacks on his resume, the hope was that Beck could unlock highly touted ( and highly paid, via NIL ) sophomore Bryce Underwood. Yet Underwood struggled, completing 58% of his passes for 924 yards, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions before being benched for freshman Tommy Carr .

Carr hasn't fared much better in his five games, throwing for 641 yards, 2 TDs and 3 INTs while completing 67% of his passes. That would appear to indicate that Michigan's offensive woes are systemic, rather than an issue with quarterback play.

Perhaps most baffling is the Wolverines' ineffectiveness in running the football. Jordan Marshall and Bryson Kuzdzal returned for this season, along with five-star prospect Savion Hiter, rated by On3 as the nation's top running back recruit . Yet Michigan currently ranks No. 109 in total rushing yards and 128.7 yards per game.

Beck's scheme, often employing a "Rhino" package with six offensive linemen , was also heavily criticized. Backs would be asked to run wide, rather than utilize a power rushing attack between or off the tackles.

That subpar production might also reflect poorly on Harding's offensive line coaching, which doesn't necessarily bode well for improvement over Michigan's next three games (at Oregon, versus UCLA and at Ohio State).

articles.body: El seleccionador nacional, Jesús Velasco, tras valorar la gran victoria de España en la 'Finalissima' ante Brasil (0-3) se quejó amargamente de que la competición sólo haya podido ser vista a través de los canales oficiales de la Federación Española de Fútbol: "Es una vergüenza que Teledeporte no haya televisado esto". Asume no obstante el hueco que ocupa el fútbol sala en el panorama audiovisual: "Tenemos que reconocer que somos lo que somos, pero somos fútbol, queremos el apoyo del fútbol, y creo que en estos partidos hemos hecho honor al fútbol sala". Fue muy crítico con la batalla que fue la semifinal de la madrugada del viernes entre Brasil y Argentina: "Esto no es una pelea como lo que se pudo ver el viernes en la otra semifinal. Todos queremos ser profesionales, queremos tener la atención de las teles, que lleguen patrocinadores. Hablo del partido de hoy que ojalá sirva para que el fútbol sala, un deporte técnico, reciba el apoyo que merece".

articles.title: Will College Football Playoff committee drop LSU Tigers out of playoff picture after blowout loss?
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's SEC propaganda campaign paid off as the first College Football Playoff poll overranked conference teams, sparking outrage from rivals.
articles.body: The release of the first College Football Playoff poll recently was treated with shock, disdain, and outright anger from many fans across the sport. Unless they root for the SEC. SEC teams were shockingly, and consistently overrepresented and overranked, to the point that prominent rival coaches openly speculated about a connection between ESPN, the SEC, and the committee's willingness to abandon any pretense of objectivity. Defending national champion Curt Cignetti, as one example, was blunt about his perception of the committee's bias. TIM BRANDO JOINS DAN DAKICH ON 'DON'T @ ME' TO DISCUSS INDIANA COACH CURT CIGNETTI'S CFP 'BIAS' COMMENTS "SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum," he said. "That's why you see all these SEC teams up there, and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high. But like I said, it's all going to be played out on the field." "Come on. These people, and there’s a whole bunch of them, they march out of the tent, and they’re given instructions on what to say," he added. "And they follow the company line. Right, and I don’t need to go any further." There's little doubt that the SEC's marketing efforts have been extremely effective at ensuring voters ignore results and focus on perception instead. And the biggest winner might have been the conference's most effective marketer: LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. Kiffin has been loudly decrying the conference's move to nine games, correctly realizing that the extra losses , which put the SEC on equal footing with the Big Ten and Big 12, will be tough to overcome when evaluating resumes. To combat this, he's spent most of the past year campaigning for the benefit of the committee. Saying, incorrectly, that the SEC is Just Different and deserves to be treated like special snowflakes relative to other conferences. "The conferences are so different," he said recently. "They are. They’re different stadiums, they’re different environments, they’re different middle to bottom of them. So you’re not playing equal schedules, they’re not even close. If you took an SEC team and gave them another one of those conference’s schedules, they’d average two more wins. Well, that’s a big deal. So, I say all that to say you had to go to more teams, because the system’s broke in how they pick them." Pretty much all of that is wrong. But his propaganda efforts, based on the first week's poll, clearly worked. Losses in the SEC simply don't matter as much as they should, a trend that was obvious in 2025 when the Alabama Crimson Tide were blown out by Georgia in the conference championship game and didn't drop a single spot. The committee decided ahead of time that they should be in, so they determined that the SEC Championship Game could only help the winner, and not hurt the loser. Will that same preferential treatment be given to the loser of a, say, Utah-BYU Big 12 Championship Game? Of course not. Because of the stadiums or something. Returning to Kiffin's diatribe though, one stat that he curiously never brings up is the SEC's recent performance when the games actually matter. And unfortunately for him and them, it's not very good. In 2025-2026, the SEC went 1-8 in bowl games. They were 0-3 in the College Football Playoff against non-SEC P4 opponents. Texas A&M went 7-1 in the SEC and was a tiebreaker away from reaching the conference championship game, then scored all of three points against a lowly Miami Hurricanes team at home. In their awe-inspiring temple of an SEC stadium. Houston beat LSU in their bowl game. Virginia beat Missouri. Illinois beat Tennessee. Iowa beat Vanderbilt. Then Alabama, the team gifted a spot in the playoff thanks to their conference patch, was obliterated by Indiana 38-3 in the Rose Bowl. So two of the top three teams in the SEC, Texas A&M and Alabama, lost their non-SEC playoff games by a combined score of 48-6. Six points combined. "They're not even close." "They'd average two more wins." And people actually believe this stuff. Since the expanded playoff format started, SEC teams are 2-5 against other P4 conference teams. They're 5-7 overall, while the Big Ten is 8-5. "They're not even close." There's another part of Kiffin's ridiculous posturing that he never brings up: travel. This isn't the SEC's fault, of course, but the conference's geographic alignment gives them a tremendous advantage over the Big Ten or ACC. LSU is in the Central Time Zone. Of their 12 games, just two were or are scheduled for any other time zone, Kentucky and Tennessee. They already lost to the Wildcats. USC, by contrast, plays four games in other time zones, including three in the Eastern Time Zone. USC, despite being based in Los Angeles, plays more times in the Eastern Time Zone than LSU does. UCLA has six games in time zones other than its home Pacific time zone. That's a massive advantage for the Tigers and for most SEC teams. Their travel schedules simply don't match up to the grueling gauntlet of the Big Ten. Just imagine how many more losses Kiffin and his marketing group would have if they had to travel like their peers. But stadiums or something. This isn't the first time the SEC boosters have done their fake superiority performance. And yet they learn nothing from it. December 2024 - Lane Kiffin: "The SEC is just different, it's totally different. You might as well be in different leagues, not different conferences, different leagues." June 2025 - Vanderbilt QB Diego Pavia: "You want to play with the best — you don’t want to play with the Big Ten. … You ignore those calls." July 2025 - Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko: "It’s a gauntlet going into the SEC season." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE October 2025 - Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer: "This is our third game in a row in the conference against a ranked opponent. That’s life in the SEC." October 2025 - Paul Finebaum: "I’d like to see Indiana go through the gauntlet that Alabama has gone through…" November 2025 - Lane Kiffin: "Texas A&M being [No.] 3 — what more do you want them to do to be [No.] 1?" THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! December 2025 - SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey: "I actually think we deserve seven in," he said referring to the number of SEC teams that should be in the playoff. "I think the seven teams that are in the top-14, half of the top 14 teams are from the SEC. That's an indication that this league is different, the expectations are different, the competition is different, and the rewards should respect each of those elements." December 2025 - Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea: "This should be about the 12 best teams in the country and a 10-2 team in the SEC … look, obviously we love our league. It just means more here and all that kind of stuff, but there’s a level of respect that needs to be held for the gauntlet we’ve been through and how we’ve met the match and done the things we need to do," Lea told OutKick. "I mean, it is just absurd the idea that we’re going to open the door to teams that play in conferences that aren’t the SEC that have the same record we have. I mean, it’s crazy." December 2025 - Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian: "If you really look at the body of work, and you look at the Southeastern Conference of what we have to go through every week, you look at the non-conference schedule we played, to go to Ohio State in Week 1 and lose by seven when we outgained them by nearly 200 yards—we got a really good football team. It would be a disservice to our sport if this team is not a playoff team when we went and scheduled that non-conference game." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER December 2025 - Alabama QB Ty Simpson: "In general, we think that... actually we know we have the best offense in the country." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD This is why it's so galling that the committee listened to Kiffin and Sankey and Sark and the relentless propaganda: it's just wrong. It's been proven wrong. It is not accurate. Kiffin's Tigers were blown out by Alabama on Saturday night, to the point where their awe-inspiring stadium was mostly empty halfway through the fourth quarter. Will the committee keep them without shouting distance of the top-12? Or will they do what they would to another team and conference, and drop the Tigers to the bottom of the top 25 or out of it entirely? This is why Kiffin made these comments, because he hoped that the standards will be lower for him than they are for other schools. Lose three times? It's because of stadiums or some nonsense. Lose four times? It's because of Nick Saban in 2015. There can never be consequences for the SEC, because they're just special. Kiffin's right, the system they use to select teams is broken. We'll just have to see how broken, in his favor, it actually is.

articles.title: Gotham FC head coach apologizes for poor pitch quality at Sports Illustrated Stadium after NWSL quarterfinal win over Seattle Reign
articles.summary: Gotham was reportedly fined $10,000 by the league for the field's conditions during last week's regular-season finale — with the team set to host again in th...
articles.body:
Gotham FC's NWSL quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign was colored by glaring issues with the field quality — with the team set to host next week's semifinal on the same surface.

Throughout Gotham's 1-0 win on Sunday , there were clear issues with the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, where Gotham has played since 2020. Large sections of grass were worn out, with sand visible in the corners and in front of the goals.

After the loss, Reign head coach Laura Harvey did not hold back when speaking about the field quality on the broadcast. Harvey said that the league had fined Gotham $10,000 for the field's poor quality during the team's regular-season finale last week , with multiple outlets later confirming the fine.

"Let's be real, there's no way a playoff game should be played on that s***," Harvey said. "I just can't believe they've allowed it. They knew it last week."

Postgame, Gotham head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said in a news conference that the franchise did its best to get the field to improve the pitch quality, but that it had fallen short of acceptable expectations.

"I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch. I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league we should be having a better surface," Amorós said. Gotham "did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that that was the case. Unfortuantely, it wasn't. But luckily it looks like nobody got hurt."

Players from both teams also expressed their dissatisfaction with the pitch quality. Gotham defender Jess Carter said postgame the field "was so bad," while Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the pitch "atrocious," via ESPN .

"It's pretty sandy out there and a little unstable," Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell said, via ESPN. "I want to be able to give my all to the team, and everything I've got, so obviously, you can't think about that. The other team has to play on that, too."

Gotham, like many NWSL teams, is a tenant in the stadium and does not control operations in its home venue; that duty goes to MLS team New York Red Bulls. Sports Illustrated Stadium hosted a Red Bulls game on Saturday and a rugby match last week, which only degraded the pitch quality after last weekend's fine.

Gotham, as the No. 1 overall seed, will host a semifinal at Sports Illustrated Stadium next weekend, meaning another high-stakes game played on the pitch. The Red Bulls, who failed to make the MLS playoffs, will be playing a friendly against Club América the day before.

Gotham announced this summer that it will be moving to the new Etihad Park in Queens in 2028; the stadium, which is set to open next year, will be owned and operated by New York City FC.

NWSL pitch quality has come up as an issue in the past, particularly with shared venues like San Diego Wave's Snapdragon Stadium. The field quality at Snapdragon was heavily criticized ahead of the 2023 NWSL Final, with retiring Reign star Megan Rapinoe suffering an Achilles injury during the match in what was her final professional game. In 2024, the Wave relocated its final game of the season due to the degraded field.

On Sunday, Gotham ended up with the win after forcing an early Reign own goal, managing to get the win without a single shot on target.

"Obviously, it was not the best football match you will ever see, that's for sure. It's not the best football match that we've ever played, that's for sure. But we found a way to win," Amorós said postgame.

Gotham will host the No. 4-seeded Kansas City Current in the semis, on the way to defending their 2025 NWSL championship.

images.caption: Reign goalkeeper Claudia Dickey makes a save during the match, on a visibly degraded field in Sports Illustrated Stadium. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS)

articles.title: Lions' Dan Campbell comments on Christian Mahogany absence vs Dolphins
articles.summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell commented on Christian Mahogany's absence against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
One of the surprises on Sunday was the Detroit Lions starting Miles Frazier in place of Christian Mahogany at left guard.

Mahogany was sorely missed as Frazier struggled through a rough day. In its initial set of grades, Frazier received a 31.9 overall offensive grade from Pro Football Focus . According to PFF, the 6-foot-6, 325-pound offensive lineman out of LSU finished with a 48.8 pass blocking grade and a team-worst 37.8 run blocking grade.

Afterwards, Lions head coach Dan Campbell explained why Frazier earned the start in place of Mahogany.

"Well, that was team rules (with) Mahogany. It was really that simple. Miles deserved his opportunity, and so he got it. It doesn't mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today," Campbell said of the decision in his postgame news conference.

Mahogany did play five special teams snaps against the Dolphins .

It was a tough day for Frazier, it was a tough day for the Lions' offensive line, and for Detroit's offense in general. Jared Goff was sacked three times and the Lions found the end zone just once.

The Lions finished with a season-low 270 total yards of offense. But, Detroit topped Miami, 19-9, and improved to 6-2 in the process.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Reveals What Jack Campbell Said During Emotional Hospital Visit
articles.summary: Dan Campbell reveals what Jack Campbell told him in the hospital and explains why he avoided discussing football with the injured Lions linebacker.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions picked up an emotional 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but head coach Dan Campbell had something far more important on his mind following the game. After visiting injured linebacker Jack Campbell in the hospital earlier in the week, Detroit's head coach shared new details about their conversation and the remarkable determination his defensive captain continues to display.

And if there's one thing that became clear from Dan Campbell's comments, it's that Jack hasn't lost the mentality that made him one of the Lions' most respected leaders. Even while recovering from a frightening neck injury, the 26-year-old linebacker is already thinking about the challenges ahead.

Dan Campbell Reveals What Jack Told Him in Hospital

Before Sunday's game, a CBS sideline report revealed that Jack had delivered a powerful message to his head coach during a hospital visit. Despite everything he has been through, the injured linebacker reportedly expressed his determination to return to football.

"Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back," Jack reportedly told Dan Campbell, according to the CBS sideline report .

Following Detroit's victory over Miami, Dan Campbell was asked about those comments and whether he was surprised by Jack's mindset. His answer revealed just how well he knows the player who has become the heart of his defense.

"Are you surprised by anything from Jack?" Campbell responded, according to his postgame comments . "That's Jack. Jack is all about the goal in front of me, and, 'I'm going to attack that goal, and I'm going to destroy that goal, and I'll move onto the next thing.'"

That's a pretty incredible description of a player facing one of the most challenging moments of his life. And judging by Dan Campbell's reaction, Jack's determination doesn't surprise anyone who knows him personally.

Dan Campbell Says He Avoided Talking Football

Perhaps the most revealing part of Dan Campbell's comments came when he explained what he intentionally avoided discussing during his hospital visit. While Jack was apparently thinking about the football field, his head coach had a different priority.

"Anything that came (up about football), that was him. I didn't bring anything about that up, me personally," Campbell explained.

That distinction is important, especially with so many fans understandably wondering whether Jack will eventually return to the field. Dan Campbell wasn't visiting his linebacker to discuss game plans, defensive assignments, or a potential comeback.

He was there to support someone who means an enormous amount to the organization. And while the competitive side of Jack Campbell clearly remains strong, his health and recovery continue to take priority over football.

As we previously reported , Jack's message about taking care of the team until his return was revealed before Sunday's game. Dan Campbell's latest remarks provide additional insight into the conversation and how the coach views his injured captain.

Lions Deliver Emotional Victory for No. 46

While Jack continues recovering, his teammates made sure he remained part of Sunday's game in spirit. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard and Detroit's linebackers arrived at Hard Rock Stadium wearing No. 46 jerseys, sending a powerful message of support.

The Lions then backed up that gesture with an impressive defensive performance, holding Miami without a touchdown in the 19-9 victory. Detroit's defense surrendered just 182 total yards, helping the team secure its fourth consecutive win.

As we previously detailed , Aidan Hutchinson also delivered a heartfelt message to Jack following the victory. The support surrounding Detroit's defensive captain has been evident throughout an incredibly emotional week.

Meanwhile, Jack has already shared an encouraging update on his recovery , revealing that he has full movement in his lower body and continues making progress with movement in his upper body. Although those developments are encouraging, no timetable for a return to football has been established.

Dan Campbell knows Jack Campbell better than most, and his latest comments make it clear that the linebacker's determination hasn't changed despite a frightening injury. The same competitive mindset that helped Jack become a leader of Detroit's defense is now guiding him through a much more important personal challenge.

But perhaps the most meaningful detail from Sunday's comments was Dan Campbell's admission that he didn't bring up football during their hospital conversation. He understands that his player's health comes first, regardless of how badly Jack might want to get back on the field.

Those two words from Dan Campbell say just about everything you need to know about his defensive captain. And while Lions fans will undoubtedly be rooting for No. 46 to make a full recovery, the most important victory right now has nothing to do with football.

articles.title: Kentucky vs. Kansas Basketball preview: The Tyran Stokes matchup, game info, and predictions
articles.summary: We break down the Tyran Stokes drama, key matchups, odds and game predictions for Kentucky Wildcats vs. Kansas Jayhawks.
articles.body:
Kentucky Basketball has the game Big Blue Nation has been looking forward to all offseason. The Wildcats head to Chicago to face the Kansas Jayhawks Tuesday in the Champions Classic.

With two early-season tune-ups out of the way, Mark Pope and his squad will face their first true test of the year against Bill Self's loaded roster. Both blue-blood programs have highly revamped rosters, making this early-season clash a massive measuring stick for both teams.

One of the biggest storylines in this matchup is Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes. Stokes was the clear No. 1 prospect in the 2026 recruiting class. In late April 2026, he committed to Kansas over Kentucky and Oregon, ending a massive, high-profile recruiting battle.

Kentucky's staff essentially put all its chips on landing the Louisville native, which ultimately backfired. By focusing so heavily on Stokes, the Wildcats let other top-10 prospects like Caleb Holt and Christian Collins slip away to other programs.

Adding fuel to the rivalry fire, sources reported that Stokes had actually signed paperwork with Kansas a month before making his public commitment.

This means he took his spring visit to Lexington and spent a night shooting around at Rupp Arena, knowing full well he was going to be a Jayhawk.

But Stokes isn't the only danger on this Jayhawk roster.

The Jayhawks are rolling into Chicago 2-0 and with plenty of momentum. Kansas recently demolished the Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 89-45 on November 6. The Jayhawks' defense smothered MTSU, holding them to 25% shooting, while their offense operated with elite efficiency, hitting nearly 63% of their shots.

In that blowout win, Stokes looked comfortable in Bill Self's system, playing 21 minutes and recording 8 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists. Trey Kaufman-Renn had 17 and will test Kentucky's power forward position.

Another Kentucky native, Taylen Kinney, will be interested in showing up against his home state school, too.

Kansas, like Kentucky, has had 2 tune-up games against Fordham and MTSU. So this will be a big step up in talent, too.

How will Tyran Stokes handle the pressure? Emotions will be high on both sides. Stokes is suiting up against the home-state team he spurned. Will Stokes let the narrative get to him, or will the top-ranked freshman rise to the occasion under the bright lights of the Champions Classic?

Can Kentucky avoid a slow start against elite competition? Kentucky has struggled with slow starts under Mark Pope in seasons prior. A team like Kansas will not let you back into the game if you surrender a 10-point lead in the first five minutes.

Who wins the backcourt battle? Kentucky needs Zoom Diallo and Alex Wilkins to limit turnovers and play efficiently. Kansas features a dynamic, highly recruited backcourt that can defend the perimeter fiercely. If Kentucky's guards can navigate the Kansas pressure and feed the shooters who need to keep hitting triples at a high clip, the Wildcats and Jayhawks will be close all night long. If the turnovers pile up, the deficit might too.

This is exactly the type of game that defines early-season college basketball. Kentucky will need a full 40-minute effort to take down Kansas. Kansas will want to prove just how good they are, and Mark Pope will look to get a win to show this team is different than last year's.

The frontcourt battle will also be critical.

Malachi Moreno will need to have a big game against a deep Kansas frontcourt for Kentucky to have a chance. If Moreno can hold his own inside and the Wildcats hit their 3s, Kentucky can win.

However, the Jayhawks are deeper and have the nation's best freshman leading the charge.

Game Time: Approximately 9:30 PM ET, though it usually ends up being closer to 10 since it doesn't start until 30 minutes after the Duke – Michigan State game ends.

Location: United Center in Chicago, Illinois (Champions Classic)

Online Stream: Watch ESPN and the ESPN app

Radio: UK Sports Network with Tom Leach and Jack "Goose" Givens

Odds : Kansas is favored in early projections, like at DraftKings, where the Jayhawks are a 5.5-point favorite with an expected over/under hovering around 152.5. KenPom (73%), BartTorvik (73%), and Evan Miya (79%) all favor the Jayhawks to win.

Predictions: KenPom metrics suggest an 83-76 win for Kansas. BartTorvik has the Jayhawks winning 81-74. Evan Miya is right there too, projecting Kansas to win 81-72.

As for me, I expect a back-and-forth battle where Kentucky's shooting keeps them in it until the final media timeout. I worry a lot about the defense; Kansas has some elite athletes, and turnovers are still a concern. I think Momcilovic will be the talisman here; if he can get 20+, I think Kentucky wins. If not, Kansas does. I think he gets there and it leads to a big 87-83 victory, Kentucky!

What will you be watching for in this Champions Classic matchup? How do you see the Tyran Stokes dynamic playing out? Send us your thoughts in the comments section!

articles.title: La escuela de Las Rozas
articles.standfirst: De los 27 convocados por De la Fuente, 23 pasaron por las inferiores
articles.summary: De los 27 convocados por De la Fuente, 23 pasaron por las inferiores
articles.body: La selección española se concentra esta tarde en su casa de Las Rozas para poner punto y final a un 2026 memorable. Por delante, dos partidos, ante Chequia, el jueves en el Letná de Praga, y el domingo, en el Metropolitano, con Inglaterra como rival, para saber si los cuartos de final de la Nations League los afronta con, en cualquier caso, la ida en Mestalla y la vuelta en casa o fuera. España se concentra con 27 jugadores llamados a filas, pendiente de la incorporación de David Raya y del asunto burocrático que le mantiene en Londres. De esos 27 futbolistas llamados a filas por Luis de la Fuente, sólo hay cuatro que no han pasado por las categorías inferiores de la selección: dos porteros, (Raya y Valles), De Frutos, y un jugador nacido fuera de España, Laporte. El modelo de trabajo que se lleva a cabo en Las Rozas hace tiempo que es la mejor vía de acceso a la absoluta. Era una cadena poderosa en las categorías inferiores, pero que después se rompía al llegar a la absoluta. Desde 2008, el cambio ha sido tan radical que España se ha convertido en una selección ganadora en todos los escalones. Y lo hace con una estructura propia, en la que la llegada a la selección absoluta desde las categorías inferiores es constante. Para Luis de la Fuente, que también es producto de la pirámide de la selección, nutrir a la absoluta desde la escalera de formación es su modus operandi. Rara vez una de sus elecciones llega a través de jugadores que no se han fogueado en las inferiores. El seleccionador encuentra en ellos zonas de seguridad, jugadores que apenas necesitan ser informados de lo que se busca, de lo que se plantea. Por ahí viene la elección en esta convocatoria de Marc Roca. El pivote del Betis no pisaba Las Rozas desde mayo de 2019, cuando fue el elegido para el eje del equipo campeón de Europa en Italia ante la renuncia de Rodri. De la Fuente ha optado por esa vía antes que por la de llamar a Luis Milla, brillante en el Como. Es una posición delicada y prefiere la seguridad de quien conoce qué respuestas se buscan. Los tres capitanes para esta ventana, Unai Simón, Ferran y Oyarzabal, son claros ejemplos de ese modelo. Los tres han llegado desde las categorías inferiores y los tres han sido campeones arriba y abajo. En la lista hay seis campeones olímpicos (Joan García, Pubill, Barrios, Baena, Fermín y Cubarsí), y la cifra se va a la docena si se cuenta a los que fueron plata en 2021. Un ejemplo.

articles.title: Hoy se desvela el Golden Boy… y todas las miradas apuntan a Cubarsí
articles.standfirst: ‘Tuttosport’ desvela este mediodía quién recogerá el testigo de Désiré Doué como el mejor futbolista sub21 de Europa • Clara Serrajordi, entre las favoritas en la categoría femenina
articles.summary: ‘Tuttosport’ desvela este mediodía quién recogerá el testigo de Désiré Doué como el mejor futbolista sub21 de Europa • Clara Serrajordi, entre las favoritas en la categoría femenina
articles.body: Descubrir a la próxima estrella del futuro se ha convertido en la gran obsesión del fútbol actual. Eso es, precisamente, lo que lleva realizando la revista ‘Tuttosport’ desde que implantó el ‘Golden Boy Award’ en 2003 para premiar al mejor futbolista menor de 21 años militante en un club europeo. Hoy, en la ciudad de Sassuolo (Italia) y con MARCA como miembro de un jurado formado por 50 periodistas, se desvela quién recoge el testigo de Désiré Doué… y todas las miradas apuntan a Pau Cubarsí (Estanyol, 2007). El pasado mes de octubre, en un acto que tuvo lugar en Venecia, se dieron a conocer los 25 finalistas (20+5 ‘wild cards’) de una lista inicial de 100 nombres. Entre ellos, eso sí, no figuraba un Lamine Yamal que ya fue condecorado en 2024. Y es que, a pesar de estar todavía en edad (19 años) de recibir el premio, las normas establecidas desde su fundación dictan que ningún ganador previo puede volver a ser reelegido. No será hasta diciembre, eso sí, cuando el ganador recoja el premio en Turín. Pau Cubarsí, pieza clave en la conquista del Mundial por parte de España, además de haber levantado Liga y Supercopa con el Barcelona el curso pasado, lleva meses encabezando una lista en la que también figuran nombres como Ayyoub Bouaddi (Manchester City/Marruecos), Warren Zaïre-Emery (PSG/Francia), Yan Diomande (Real Madrid/Costa de Marfil) o Lennart Karl (Bayern Múnich/Alemania). El central culé, en cualquier caso, no es el único representante español que aspira a llevarse un galardón que, previamente, ya han ganado Cesc Fàbregas, Isco Alarcón, Pedri González, Gavi y el propio Lamine Yamal. Le acompañan Marc Bernal y Xavi Espart, sus compañeros de quinta desde La Masía, y Jon Martín, ya indiscutible en una Real Sociedad que ganó la Copa del Rey. Fueron, además, pareja de centrales en las inferiores de la Selección antes de que Cubarsí diese el salto a la Absoluta. No hay país con mayor representación. Todos los premios: Además del Golden Boy, ‘Tuttosport’ también premiará al mejor talento del fútbol italiano, con Pío Esposito (Inter de Milán) como vigente ganador, además del Golden Boy Web, el cual es elegido por los internautas como resultado de una votación popular. Christos Mouzakitis (Hull City) fue reconocido en la pasada edición. A su vez, también se entregará el Absolute Golden Boy. El año anterior, como reconociendo tras su fallecimiento, se eligió a Diogo Jota. También hay premios para el mejor club, presidente o representante. Si todas las miradas apuntan a Pau Cubarsí para llevarse el Golden Boy… sería una sorpresa que alguna de las tres nominadas del Barcelona no se llevase el premio en la categoría femenina. Galardón que Vicky López ya se llevó en 2024, haciendo ‘doblete’ con Lamine Yamal, y que reconoció a Michelle Agyemang (Arsenal) en la última edición. Clara Serrajordi (2007) es quien tienen más papeletas para sucederla. A sus apenas 19 años, ya está asentada en las filas de un Barcelona que conquistó el triplete de Liga, Copa y Champions la temporadas pasada. Además, derribó las puertas de la Selección… llegando a levantar la Nations League y certificando la clasificación al Mundial de este verano. Entre el resto de 10 nominadas se encuentran sus compañeras Sydney Schertenleib (2007), también integrante en el primera equipo, y Giulia Galli (2008), incorporada para el filial desde la Roma… además de Felicia Schröder (2007), fichada por el Real Madrid este pasado verano tras ganar la Europa Cup con el Häcken la temporada pasada.
